vn: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
rk: Combine a prior knowledge graph that is periodically updated by an online-built current knowledge graph (embedded via GCN) with scene features fed into a transformer, and train an A3C (LSTM+MLP) policy for goal-oriented navigation. The abstract reports that the knowledge graph significantly improves navigation performance and improves generalization to novel scenes and novel objects. No ablation details or numbers are available, since only the abstract was provided.

t: Instance-aware Exploration-Verification-Exploitation for Instance ImageGoal Navigation
ab: As a new embodied vision task, Instance ImageGoal Navigation (IIN) aims to navigate to a specified object depicted by a goal image in an unexplored environment. The main challenge of this task lies in identifying the target object from different viewpoints while rejecting similar distractors. Existing ImageGoal Navigation methods usually adopt the simple Exploration-Exploitation framework and ignore the identification of specific instance during navigation. In this work, we propose to imitate the human behaviour of ``getting closer to confirm" when distinguishing objects from a distance. Specifically, we design a new modular navigation framework named Instance-aware Exploration-Verification-Exploitation (IEVE) for instance-level image goal navigation. Our method allows for active switching among the exploration, verification, and exploitation actions, thereby facilitating the agent in making reasonable decisions under different situations. On the challenging HabitatMatterport 3D semantic (HM3D-SEM) dataset, our method surpasses previous state-of-the-art work, with a classical segmentation model (0.684 vs. 0.561 success) or a robust model (0.702 vs. 0.561 success)
tl: IEVE modularly switches among exploration, verification (approaching to confirm) and exploitation to identify goal instances for Instance ImageGoal Navigation on HM3D.
rk: Add an active Verification stage between exploration and exploitation, with a switch policy that uses the number of matched keypoints and the agent-to-candidate distance to decide whether to explore, verify (approach) or exploit (confirmed target). Matching reliability drops sharply with distance (Fig. 7: TP rate collapses at the hard/far level for high thresholds), so a fixed threshold either rejects true targets or accepts false ones. The EVE switch beats a fixed-threshold Exploration-Exploitation policy (Tab. 2: 0.666 vs 0.590 Success with Mask RCNN; 0.684 vs 0.620 with SwinTrans). The GT-perception upper bound of 0.850 shows perception is the remaining bottleneck.

t: RoboCodeX: Multimodal Code Generation for Robotic Behavior Synthesis
ab: Robotic behavior synthesis, the problem of understanding multimodal inputs and generating precise physical control for robots, is an important part of Embodied AI. Despite successes in applying multimodal large language models for high-level understanding, it remains challenging to translate these conceptual understandings into detailed robotic actions while achieving generalization across various scenarios. In this paper, we propose a tree-structured multimodal code generation framework for generalized robotic behavior synthesis, termed RoboCodeX. RoboCodeX decomposes high-level human instructions into multiple object-centric manipulation units consisting of physical preferences such as affordance and safety constraints, and applies code generation to introduce generalization ability across various robotics platforms. To further enhance the capability to map conceptual and perceptual understanding into control commands, a specialized multimodal reasoning dataset is collected for pre-training and an iterative self-updating methodology is introduced for supervised fine-tuning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RoboCodeX achieves state-of-the-art performance in both simulators and real robots on four different kinds of manipulation tasks and one navigation task.
tl: Tree-structured multimodal code generation for robotic behavior synthesis, fine-tuned MLLM; mainly manipulation with one navigation task.
rk: Train a BLIP-2-style vision-language model (EVA-CLIP ViT-G + Q-Former + LLaMA-13B) to generate tree-of-thought robot code. The code decomposes an instruction into object-centric units, and each unit calls perception, affordance, articulation, grasp-preference and motion-planning APIs. Training uses GPT-4-synthesized code and an iterative self-updating SFT loop driven by execution search. The gains over GPT-4V on manipulation come mainly from better physical grounding (grasp preference, articulation direction) rather than better task decomposition. The failure analysis (Fig. errorbar) shows both RoboCodeX and GPT-4V decompose long-horizon tasks correctly; most errors come from suboptimal gras

t: NaVid: Video-based VLM Plans the Next Step for Vision-and-Language Navigation
ab: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) stands as a key research problem of Embodied AI, aiming at enabling agents to navigate in unseen environments following linguistic instructions. In this field, generalization is a long-standing challenge, either to out-of-distribution scenes or from Sim to Real. In this paper, we propose NaVid, a video-based large vision language model (VLM), to mitigate such a generalization gap. NaVid makes the first endeavor to showcase the capability of VLMs to achieve state-of-the-art level navigation performance without any maps, odometers, or depth inputs. Following human instruction, NaVid only requires an on-the-fly video stream from a monocular RGB camera equipped on the robot to output the next-step action. Our formulation mimics how humans navigate and naturally gets rid of the problems introduced by odometer noises, and the Sim2Real gaps from map or depth inputs. Moreover, our video-based approach can effectively encode the historical observations of robots as spatio-temporal contexts for decision making and instruction following. We train NaVid with 510k navigation samples collected from continuous environments, including action-planning and instruction-reasoning samples, along with 763k large-scale web data. Extensive experiments show that NaVid achieves state-of-the-art performance in simulation environments and the real world, demonstrating superior cross-dataset and Sim2Real transfer. We thus believe our proposed VLM approach plans the next step for not only the navigation agents but also this research field.
tl: Video-based VLM taking monocular RGB streams and instructions to output next-step actions, trained on 510k navigation samples plus web data, transferring to real world.
cm: Accepted by Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS 2024)
rk: Fine-tune a video VLM (LLaMA-VID with Vicuna-7B) to read the whole monocular RGB video history plus the instruction. It emits the next low-level action in language, e.g. 'move forward 75 cm' or 'turn left 30 degrees'. Training co-mixes R2R-CE oracle and DAgger step samples, instruction-reasoning samples, and web video QA data. Representing history as compressed video tokens is far better than text or map summaries. In Table V, text-based history gets 0 SR, map+text 9.13, and ego-view+text 23.5, versus 37.4 for video on R2R-CE val-unseen, and the text pipeline is about 2x slower. Co-training with web video QA data is the single most important ingredient: removing it drops SR from 37.4 to 24.7

t: When in Doubt, Think Slow: Iterative Reasoning with Latent Imagination
ab: In an unfamiliar setting, a model-based reinforcement learning agent can be limited by the accuracy of its world model. In this work, we present a novel, training-free approach to improving the performance of such agents separately from planning and learning. We do so by applying iterative inference at decision-time, to fine-tune the inferred agent states based on the coherence of future state representations. Our approach achieves a consistent improvement in both reconstruction accuracy and task performance when applied to visual 3D navigation tasks. We go on to show that considering more future states further improves the performance of the agent in partially-observable environments, but not in a fully-observable one. Finally, we demonstrate that agents with less training pre-evaluation benefit most from our approach.
tl: Training-free decision-time iterative inference refines a model-based RL agent's latent states using coherence of imagined future states, improving visual 3D navigation performance.
rk: At decision time, take gradient steps on the agent's current latent state (recurrent state h_t) to minimise an uncertainty-based objective (state or parameter information gain) computed over imagined latent rollouts, so that the state is coherent with the world model's predicted future; no training is needed. State-IG with a short rollout (lambda=1) mainly closes the amortisation gap of the current-state reconstruction. Longer rollouts (lambda=8/16) barely change the current reconstruction but shift the agent's trajectory toward states that are reconstructed more accurately, and this is clearest in partially-observable 3D tasks (Fig. natlab_trajectories).
